subject: Error in fitMeasures(object) : object 'logl.H1' not found

messages.author: 1a351e065a2c989d
messages.subject: Error in fitMeasures(object) : object 'logl.H1' not found
parts:
Dear Yves and/or Lavaan experts,

 

I’m running some fairly straightforward models, with the most notable characteristic being high intercorrelations among the MVs and many of the LVs. I recently upgraded to R 3.03 and updated my packages (which, I think, took lavaan from 0.5-14 to 0.5-16, though this might have happened earlier).

 

Now when I try to fit several models—notably, perhaps, these seem to be the ones with the larger intercorrelation issues—I get the error,

“Error in fitMeasures(object) : object 'logl.H1' not found.” From the summary() or inspect(object, “fit”) commands. I have searched (to the best of my ability) through the fit object structure trying to figure out what is wrong, but I don’t think it’s likely that I will figure it out.

 

It’s quite likely the model has problems, but I suspect this is not supposed to be the error I get. I tried downgrading to lavaan 0.5-14, but the error persisted, leading me to think that the creation of the fit object, or the operation of the inspect() function has somehow changed, or interacted with my system.

 

I am running R 3.03 on Windows (64-bit, but I believe I have this problem on a laptop running the 32-bit version, as well). My lavaan version is 0.5-16. The problem does not occur on an older Linux machine (Linux Mint); I can try to find the versions of R and lavaan there, later, if you’d like.

 

I’ve attached one of the offending models, with the data to which I’ve been trying to fit it. Any help would be appreciated.

 

Thanks,

 

Darrin L. Rogers

Department of Psychology

University of Texas-Pan American

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Error in fitMeasures(object) : object 'logl.H1' not found
parts:
On 03/14/2014 09:08 PM, Darrin Rogers wrote:
> “Error in fitMeasures(object) : object 'logl.H1' not found.”

The problem is with your data.frame ('D'). Try

str(D)

and you will see that some columns are not 'numeric', but 'matrix' (have
you used 'scale()'?).

Try

varTables(mod.efa.fm.fit)


The workaround (in <0.5.17) is to convert all 'matrix' columns to
'numeric', as follows (assuming the data.frame is called D, and all
variables are needed):

D <- as.data.frame(lapply(D, as.numeric))

and refit the model. This is 'fixed' in 0.5-17 where this will be done
automatically.

Yves.
